seo.title: Pump Head Calculator - Total Dynamic Head
seo.description: Pump head calculator for centrifugal systems — Determines total dynamic head from flow, pressure & elevation changes

formula.explanation: TDH = H_static + ΔP/(ρg) + h_friction. Engine converts kPa→Pa for the pressure term automatically.

content.introduction: Total Dynamic Head (TDH) is the total equivalent head a pump must provide to overcome elevation, system pressure, and friction losses. This is the primary parameter for selecting a pump from manufacturer curves.

faq.q: What is the difference between static head and dynamic head?
faq.a: Static head is elevation difference only. Dynamic head includes all losses: elevation + pressure + friction + velocity head.

faq.q: Do I need to add velocity head?
faq.a: Velocity head (v²/2g) is usually negligible (0.1-0.5m) compared to other heads and is omitted in most practical calculations.

faq.q: How do I convert head between meters and feet?
faq.a: Multiply meters by 3.28084 to get feet. For example, 20 m head = 65.6 ft. Pump curves are often given in feet for imperial systems and meters for metric systems, so convert before comparing.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Pump Head
sections.body:
**Head units**

- 1 m = 3.28084 ft
- 1 ft = 0.3048 m
- 1 m water head ≈ 9.81 kPa ≈ 0.0981 bar

**Pressure units**

- 1 bar = 100 kPa = 14.5038 psi
- 1 psi = 6.8948 kPa

**Flow units**

- 1 m³/h = 0.2778 L/s = 4.403 US gpm

Total dynamic head (TDH) = static head + friction head + velocity head. Keep all head terms in the same length unit (m or ft) before summing.
